chunks: Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari, from his father, said: He narrated to us Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd ibn Yaqteen, from an-Nadhr ibn Suwayd, from Yahya al-Halabi, from Ali ibn Abu Hamza, who said: I was with Abu Baseer, and with us was a freed-slave of Abu Ja'far al-Baqir, who said: I heard Abu Ja'far say: From us there are twelve narrators (muhaddithun), the seventh of us is my son al-Qa'im. Abu Baseer stood up to him and said: I bear witness that I heard Abu Ja'far saying this forty years ago. And Abu al-Hasan al-Shuja'i (may Allah have mercy on him) said: These two hadiths are among those which Abu Abdullah (may Allah have mercy on him) reviewed after he finished, and [this is] my copying of the book.

key_terms.أَبُو بَصِيرٍ: Abu Baseer (a companion of the Imams)
key_terms.الْبَاقِرُ: al-Baqir (The Splitter Openener, title of the 5th Imam)

ai.seo_question: Who is the seventh Imam and what is his title according to the hadith of the Twelve Imams?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Nu'mani’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* explicitly identifies the seventh Imam as al-Qa'im, son of the sixth, anchoring the doctrine of the Twelve Imams within the Ja'fari tradition. The inclusion of Abu Baseer’s testimony regarding the forty-year duration of this narration underscores the early and continuous transmission of this specific eschatological expectation. The scholarly note on textual transmission highlights the rigorous verification processes employed by early Shia scholars to authenticate the lineage and authority of the Imams.
